q1_issues.issue: The "whenever" trigger clause sits in the CONCLUSION instead of the premises — the only premise is (Member $k keeper), so the rule derives a spreading of ground feathers around a lit lantern for every Keeper, asserting an occurrence the sentence merely conditions on.

(Inheritance ground_feather ground) exposes a modifier genus that the compound rule licenses only for a gradable, positional or material ADJECTIVE modifier — "ground" is either a noun modifier (never exposed) or a participial adjective belonging to none of those three classes.

q2_gaps: a PARTICIPIAL modifier inside a compound kind ("ground feathers") — the fusion list (term of art / nationality / role title / material adjective) and the modifier-genus exposure list (gradable / positional / material adjective) both omit participial adjectives, so neither whether to fuse nor whether to expose the modifier is decided
notes: Roles, the two definites resolved back to the trigger's feather group and lantern, the Around / Against preposition-named obliques, the "lit" participial adjective as a separate Member atom, and the During tie are all right. The damage is confined to the premise/conclusion split.
